comments.body:
Root cause confirmed by direct reproduction against process_status on b97d414b8e2: after open->closed with all 4 close keys then closed->open, the reduced state still held force_close_reason/close_class/close_reason/completion_expectation; a following clean open->closed kept force_close_reason='bypass'. _fold_close_metadata only writes (present-only, gated on status=='closed'), and no step cleared them on leaving closed. Comparison: _clear_claimed_session already clears claim provenance on the winning in_progress exit.

Fix: new _clear_close_metadata (guard current_status=='closed' and status!='closed') called at both winner sites only; _fold_close_metadata unchanged. _REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION 7->8 so stale caches recompute. New tests/unit/test_reducer_status.py: 4 of 6 tests failed before the fix (reopen clears, clean re-close, end-to-end library force/reopen/close with forced STATUS event still in the log, v7 stale cache); the 2 fork tests (losing reopen keeps winner metadata, losing close does not overwrite) passed before and after. 64 tests across the new file, test_administrative_close_dispositions, test_processors_status_split, test_updated_at pass.

Out of scope, filed as sugarcandy-fusible-hogget: SNAPSHOT compiled_state carrying stale keys (8 closed + 4 open/in_progress SNAPSHOTs in this tracker).

compiled_state.description:
## Problem

`force_close_reason` is written when a close uses `--force=<reason>`. Nothing ever
clears it. After `rebar reopen`, the value persists onto an `open` ticket, and a later
close that passes every gate and carries a valid completion signature leaves the
original bypass text in place. The ticket then asserts two contradictory facts at once:
a signed completion-verifier PASS, and a recorded gate bypass.

The same applies to `close_class`, `close_reason`, and `completion_expectation`.

Any audit keyed on `force_close_reason` — which is exactly how a project enforces that
force did not circumvent a gate, since a forced op records no certification — reads a
properly verified close as an unverified one. There is no supported way to clear it.

Reported against nava-rebar 0.13.1 (Python 3.14.7, macOS) by a client project.

## Evidence

Reproduction, from a ticket whose commit carries a valid trailer:

```
rebar transition "$T" open closed --force="repro: bypassing the landing gate on purpose"
rebar reopen "$T"
rebar list | python3 -c "import sys,json;[print(t['status'], repr(t.get('force_close_reason'))) for t in json.load(sys.stdin) if t['ticket_id']=='$T']"

git commit -q --amend -m "Change feature.py

rebar-ticket: $T"
rebar transition "$T" open closed
```

While the ticket is OPEN it still carries a force-close reason:

```
status            : open
force_close_reason: 'repro: bypassing the landing gate on purpose'
```

After a close that passed the landing check and the completion verifier with NO
override:

```
status            : closed
close_class       : None
close_reason      : None
force_close_reason: 'repro: bypassing the landing gate on purpose'
completion-verifier: PASS
```

## Root cause

`_fold_close_metadata` (`src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py`, ~line 69) applies four
keys under a present-only rule, and every branch only ever writes:

```python
if data.get("status") == "closed" and data.get("force_close_reason"):
    state["force_close_reason"] = data["force_close_reason"]
```

Two properties combine to produce the defect:

1. The fold is gated on `status == "closed"`, so the `closed -> open` edge that `reopen`
   emits never reaches it. `rebar reopen` is a plain alias for
   `transition <id> closed open` (`src/rebar/_commands/transition.py`, ~line 772) and
   carries no clearing step of its own.
2. Because the rule is present-only, the clean close emits a STATUS event with no
   `force_close_reason` key at all — and an absent key cannot clear a stale value.

The present-only rule is CORRECT for its stated purpose: stopping a losing concurrent
close from overwriting the fork winner's provenance. It was simply never extended to the
reopen edge, where the value should be dropped rather than preserved. Any fix must keep
that concurrency guarantee intact.

## Known affected data

The reporter states two tickets in their store were force-closed, then reopened,
remediated, and closed through the plan-review and completion-verification gates with
signed attestations. Both still carry the original bypass text, including its
now-incorrect justification. Whether previously-reduced state needs a repair pass, or
whether re-reduction from the event log is sufficient once the fold is fixed, is part of
this ticket's scope to determine. Determined below under Plan step 2.

## Plan

1. Add `_clear_close_metadata(state, data)` in `src/rebar/reducer/_processors_status.py`,
   modelled on the existing `_clear_claimed_session`, whose guard is
   `data.get("current_status") == "in_progress" and data.get("status") != "in_progress"`.
   The new guard is `data.get("current_status") == "closed" and data.get("status") != "closed"`;
   it pops `close_class`, `close_reason`, `force_close_reason`, `completion_expectation`.
   `current_status` is the STATUS event's expected-prior-status field that `process_status`
   already reads for fork detection (line 79). Call it at the two winner sites next to
   `_clear_claimed_session`; the losing-fork `else` branch never calls it.
   `_fold_close_metadata` itself stays present-only and unchanged.
2. Existing stores have two persisted reduced forms, handled differently:
   - The per-ticket reducer cache, keyed on `_REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION` in
     `src/rebar/reducer/_cache.py` ("Increment it whenever projection semantics change").
     Bump it 7 -> 8 so every cached state is recomputed from the events after the latest
     SNAPSHOT. For a ticket with no SNAPSHOT, that is the whole log, so the stale keys clear.
   - SNAPSHOT `compiled_state`. `process_snapshot` copies it verbatim and replay skips the
     retired source events, so a SNAPSHOT taken after a forced close + reopen keeps the
     stale keys and this fold change cannot reach them. Worked example from this repo's
     tracker: aabf-d89e's SNAPSHOT is `status: closed` with `force_close_reason` and
     `last_reopened_at` set, while its last closing STATUS event has no force reason; 8
     such closed SNAPSHOTs and 4 open/in_progress ones exist. Repairing them requires
     rewriting SNAPSHOTs in the shared tracker (`rebuild_snapshot_from_full_log`), a
     store mutation with a clean scope boundary, so it is split to bug
     sugarcandy-fusible-hogget (df72-d570-8c77-44d4, linked discovered_from). This ticket
     does NOT claim to repair compacted tickets.

## Acceptance Criteria
- [x] Force-close (`open -> closed` with `force_close_reason="bypass"`, `close_class`,
  `close_reason`, `completion_expectation` all set), then reopen (`closed -> open`): the
  reduced state has none of the 4 keys. Asserted in `tests/unit/test_reducer_status.py`.
- [x] A later `open -> closed` with no close metadata yields `status == "closed"` and no
  `force_close_reason` key. Asserted end to end through the library (`rebar.transition`
  on a temp store, `force=` then `reopen`, then a clean close) in the same file.
- [x] Deleting the new clearing call makes both tests above fail (observed red before the
  fix; recorded in the commit message).
- [x] Concurrency: a losing fork event `closed -> open` (larger UUID than the winner)
  leaves the winner's `force_close_reason` in place, and a losing `* -> closed` fork does
  not overwrite the winner's close metadata. Asserted in the new file; the existing
  `test_fold_close_metadata_*` tests in `tests/unit/test_administrative_close_dispositions.py`
  and `test_status_fold_replay_equivalence` in `tests/unit/test_processors_status_split.py`
  pass unchanged.
- [x] A reducer cache entry written under version 7 holding a stale `force_close_reason`
  for an uncompacted (no SNAPSHOT) ticket is ignored after the bump: reducing that ticket
  dir returns state without the key. Asserted in the new file.
- [x] SNAPSHOT-carried stale keys are explicitly out of scope and tracked in
  sugarcandy-fusible-hogget; that link exists before this ticket closes.
- [x] The event log still contains the forced STATUS event with its `force_close_reason`
  after reopen: reading the ticket dir's STATUS event files back shows it.

## Testing

`tests/unit/test_reducer_status.py` does not exist yet; this ticket creates it.

```
.venv/bin/pytest tests/unit/test_reducer_status.py tests/unit/test_administrative_close_dispositions.py tests/unit/test_processors_status_split.py -p no:randomly -q
make lint && make typecheck && make verify
```

file_impact.reason: _fold_close_metadata must clear the four close keys on a winning closed->* fold while keeping the present-only concurrency guarantee
bump _REDUCER_CACHE_VERSION 7->8 so cached reduced state carrying stale close keys is invalidated and re-reduced from the event log

NEW file: regression oracle - force-close then reopen leaves no close metadata, a clean re-close reports no bypass, a losing concurrent fork does not clear or overwrite the winner, and a stale cache is re-reduced

compiled_state.title: Close metadata survives reopen, so a fully gated re-close permanently reports itself as gate-bypassed
